rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who die are taken by God after reaching maturity or before it; tawaffī denotes death and the taking of the soul.
rows.anchor: أي : يقبض روحه ويموت بعد بلوغ الأشد أو قبله والتوفي عبارة عن الموت وتوفاه الله قبض روحه

words: وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ardhal al-ʿumr is decrepit old age and senility; ʿumr is the span during which life animates the body.
rows.anchor: وهو الهرم والخرف والرذل والرذال المرغوب عنه لرداءته والعمر مدة عمارة البدن بالحياة

words: لِكَيْلَا يَعْلَمَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍۢ شَيْـًۭٔا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase describes a severe reversal of knowledge and condition: the elderly may forget what they did and knew and lose abilities, though they still know some things like a child.
rows.anchor: وهو مبالغة في انتقاض علمه وانتكاس حاله وإلا فهو يعلم بعض الأشياء كالطفل

words: لِكَيْلَا يَعْلَمَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍۢ شَيْـًۭٔا
rows.speaker: الشيخ سعدي
rows.claim: Saʿdī’s verses lament that youth and the season of life pass, warning that desire and play consume the years and youth does not return.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ سعدي قدس سره. طرب نوجوان زير مجوى كه دكر يدآب رفته بجوى

words: لِكَيْلَا يَعْلَمَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍۢ شَيْـًۭٔا
rows.speaker: النسفي
rows.claim: Al-Nasafī says ignorance before knowledge is hell because it breeds greed, whereas ignorance after knowledge is paradise because it brings acceptance and contentment.
rows.anchor: قال النسفي في "كشف الحقائق" : (أي درويش جهل يش ازعمل دوزخست وجهل بعد ازعلمبهشت

words: وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ
rows.speaker: البقلي
rows.claim: Al-Baqli reads the worst age inwardly as striving after witnessing and spiritual interruption after communion, when one loses awareness of lofty states and stations.
rows.anchor: وفي "عرائس البقلي" : ارذل العمر أيام المجاهدة بعد المشاهدة

words: وَمِنكُم مَّن يُرَدُّ إِلَىٰٓ أَرْذَلِ ٱلْعُمُرِ
rows.speaker: البقلي
rows.claim: Al-Baqli calls this God’s protective jealousy toward realized people who disclosed His secrets through excessive claims, and seeks refuge from the ego.
rows.anchor: وفي "عرائس البقلي" : ارذل العمر أيام المجاهدة بعد المشاهدة

words: وَنُقِرُّ فِى ٱلْأَرْحَامِ مَا نَشَآءُ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍۢ مُّسَمًّۭى
rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya says created beings rested in the wombs of nonexistence by God’s determination, each emerging only by His will at its anciently appointed term.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : في الآية إشارة إلى أن أطفال المكونات كانوا في أرحام

words: وَنُقِرُّ فِى ٱلْأَرْحَامِ مَا نَشَآءُ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍۢ مُّسَمًّۭى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī rejects the philosophers’ dilemma that a world beginning in time implies divine deficiency, while eternal creative causes would require an eternal world.
rows.anchor: فنقول في جوابهم إن الآية تدل على أن الله تعالى كان في الأزل

words: وَنُقِرُّ فِى ٱلْأَرْحَامِ مَا نَشَآءُ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍۢ مُّسَمًّۭى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī answers that God eternally existed alone and could create as He willed, while eternal wisdom and will fixed the world’s appointed emergence from nonexistence; before creation there was no ordinary time.
rows.anchor: فنقول في جوابهم إن الآية تدل على أن الله تعالى كان في الأزل ولم يكن معه شيء شاء وكان قادرا على إيجاد ما يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every created thing emerges from nonexistence ready for cultivation and reaches its perfection gradually; some perish before completion, while others pass beyond perfection and lose its qualities.
rows.anchor: يشير إلى أن كل طفل من أطفال المكونات يخرج من رحم العدم مستعدا للتربية وله كمال يبلغه بالتدريج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is seen as dead and dry; hāmida is like a fire that has gone out and become ashes.
rows.anchor: {وترى الارض} يا من شأنه الرؤية وهو حجة أخرى على البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revival of dead earth by rain is another proof that God can resurrect the dead and restore their scattered parts to their former state.
rows.anchor: والمعنى حسن رائق يسر ناظره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ihtazzat means that the earth moves as vegetation appears; the word suggests joyful, pleasing motion and is rarely used for an unpleasant matter.
rows.anchor: {اهتزت} تحركت بالنبات والاهتزاز الحركة الواقعة على البهجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabat means swollen, increased, and grown, from the root r-b-w; al-Qāmūs also uses it of a horse swelling from running or fright.
rows.anchor: {وربت} انتفخت وازدادت من ربا يربو ربا زاد ونما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zawj means a kind; bahīj describes beauty of color and visible delight, as when joy shows on someone’s face.
rows.anchor: {وأنابتت من كل زوج} صنف {بهيج} البهجة حسن اللون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alam tara is glossed as “did you not know,” addressing one whose characteristic is knowledge.
rows.anchor: ألم تعلم يا من من شأنه العلم

words: أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُۥ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَن فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prostration of all in heaven and earth means submission to God’s governance and will, whether beings obey willingly or are compelled.
rows.anchor: أي : ينقاد لتدبيره ومشيئته الملائكة والجن والإنس مطيعا أو عاصيا

words: أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُۥ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَن فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī distinguishes chosen prostration, for which humans are rewarded, from compelled submission; the verse uses prostration metaphorically because disbelievers, rebellious jinn, animals, and inanimates do not perform ritual worship.
rows.anchor: شبه الانقياد بأكمل أفعال المكلف في باب الطاعة وهو السجود إيذانا بكمال التسخير والتذلل وإنما حمل على المعنى المجازي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun, moon, and stars prostrate through their courses, risings, and settings that benefit people.
rows.anchor: بالسير والطلوع والغروب لمنافع العباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mountains prostrate by the springs that God runs through them and the minerals they produce.
rows.anchor: {والجبال} بإجراء الينابيع وإنبات المعادن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trees submit through shade and fruit, and animals through their wondrous construction; every creature submits in its created, sustained, healthy, or sick condition, believer or sinner.
rows.anchor: {والشجر} بالظل وحمل الثمار ونحوها {والدوآب}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many people prostrate in chosen worship; the phrase is raised by an omitted predicate, since making it governed by the preceding verb would mix literal and metaphorical senses.
rows.anchor: فهو مرتفع بمحذوف لا بالمذكور وإلا يلزم الجمع بين الحقيقة والمجاز

rows.speaker: التأويلات
rows.claim: The Taʾwīlāt says people of gnosis worship by choice, while inanimates, the unintelligent, and irreligious people submit through need.
rows.anchor: قال في "التأويلات" : أهل العرفان يسجدون سجود عبادة بالإرادة

words: أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُۥ
rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kāshifī says every atom is humble and submissive to God through the testimony of its state, which is more eloquent than speech.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (همه ذرات عالم مرخدايرا خاضع وخاشعند بدلالت حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The other multitude has punishment decreed because of disbelief and refusal to obey.
rows.anchor: بسبب كفره وإبائه عن الطاعة

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kāshifī says this is the sixth Qurʾanic prostration by scholarly consensus; the Futūḥāt calls it the prostration of witnessing and reflection, urging worshippers to join the first group and draw near.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (اين سجدة ششم است باتفاق علما ازسجدات قرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devotional couplet says the taste of prostration and obedience before God is sweeter than a hundred worldly fortunes.
rows.anchor: ذوق سجده وطاعتي يش خدا خوشتر باثيد زصد دولت ترا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī says the first multitude is small beside the second: people of beauty are fewer than people of majesty, about one in a thousand.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير : الكثير الأول كثير في نفسه بالنسبة إلى الكثير الثاني إذ أهل الجمال

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says the single person upon truth is the great majority.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه أن الواحد على الحق هو السواد الأعظم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say a group is few when counted but many when they gather and display their strength.
rows.anchor: وعن بعضهم : قليل إذا عدوا كثير إذا شدوا أي أظهروا الشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God humiliates a person whose misery He decreed eternally, according to His knowledge that the person would choose evil.
rows.anchor: {يهن الله} يهنه الله : بالفارسية(خوار كرداند) بأن كتب عليه الشقاوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one can honor such a person by granting him everlasting felicity.
rows.anchor: {فما له من مكرم} يكرمه بالسعادة إلى الأبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does as He wills, honoring or humiliating from eternity to eternity.
rows.anchor: {إن الله يفعل ما يشآء} من الإكرام والإهانة من الأزل إلى الأبد

rows.speaker: النيسابوري
rows.claim: Al-Nīsābūrī offers three reasons disbelievers outnumber believers: God shows independence from their obedience, the rarity of believers makes their honor clear, and preserving the beloved among many enemies displays divine aid.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام النيسابوري رحمه الله في "كشف الأسرار" : جعل الله الكفار أكثر من المؤمنين ليريهم أنه مستغن عن طاعتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited reports say ninety-nine of every thousand are among the people of wrath and one is taken for Paradise; another compares the people of mercy to a white hair on a black ox.
rows.anchor: وأهل الغضب تسع وتسعون من كل ألف واحد يؤخذ للجنة كما ورد في الصحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer is that the proportion concerns humans alone; when angels, houris, and youths are included, the people of mercy are more numerous than the people of wrath.
rows.anchor: قلنا هذه الكثرة بالنسبة إلى بني آدم وأما أهل الرحمة بالنسبة إليهم وإلى الملائكة والحور والغلمان فأكثر من أهل الغضب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text describes a narrowing spiritual hierarchy: most people disbelieve, then most believers sin, and the rarest reach obedience, asceticism, love, and union; the aim of creation is the perfect human.
rows.anchor: والتحقيق أن المقصود من النشآت كلها ظهور الإنسان الكامل وهو واحد كالألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rare person of union gains true honor by annihilating the self in God, the real station of prostration, and cannot be overcome even if the world seeks to humiliate him.
rows.anchor: فهو أعز من الكبريت الأحمر والمسك الأذفر وهو الذي أكرمه الله بكرامة لم يكرم بها أحدا

rows.speaker: الله
rows.claim: The sacred report says whoever opposes or harms one of God’s friends has declared war on Him; God aids His friends and leaves their opponent humiliated.
rows.anchor: ألا ترى إلى قوله : "من عادى لي وليا فقد بارزني بالمحاربة"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alladhīna ukhrijū is genitive as an adjective qualifying the relative pronoun.
rows.anchor: في حيز الجر على أنه صفة للموصول

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says the expulsion explains the injustice that permitted fighting, and their homes were Mecca.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ : لما بين أنهم إنما أذنوا في القتال لأجل أنهم ظلموا فسر ذلك الظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Countries are called diyār because people move about within them; Arabs around Mecca called themselves people of the land, meaning the country.
rows.anchor: وتسمى البلاد الديار لأنه يدار فيها للتصرف يقال : ديار بكر

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib derives dār, a dwelling, from its circuit enclosed by a wall; diyār is its plural, and a town is also called dār.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : الدار المنزل اعتبارا بدورانها الذي لها بالحائط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were expelled without a valid cause; ḥaqq is what is due or obligatory.
rows.anchor: أي خرجوا بغير موجب استحقوا الخروج فالحق مصدر قولك حق الشيء يحق بالكسر أي وجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is parsed as a substitute for ḥaqq: their only “cause” was monotheism, which should merit acceptance, not expulsion; the ironic construction resembles a line by al-Nābigha.
rows.anchor: {إلا أن يقولوا ربنا الله} بدل من حق أي بغير موجب سوى التوحيد

rows.speaker: النابغة
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha’s verse exemplifies the ironic phrasing of treating a virtue as though it were a defect: the only flaw is that their swords are nicked from battle.
rows.anchor: لكن لا على الظاهر بل على طريقة قول النابغة :

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God averts destruction by empowering believers against disbelievers in every age.
rows.anchor: بتسليط المؤمنين منهم على الكفارين في كل عصر وزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hadimmat means buildings would be torn down; tahdīm intensifies the sense of demolition, here through the polytheists’ conquest.
rows.anchor: الهدم إسقاط البناء والتهديم للتكثير أي لخربت باستيلاء المشركين

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib describes ṣawāmiʿ as pointed or tapering buildings; they were monks’ worship places, often isolated in mountains or deserts.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : الصومعة كل بناء منصمع الرأس متلاصقة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib identifies biyaʿ as Christian churches built in towns where congregations gathered to worship, unlike remote hermitages.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : الصومعة كل بناء منصمع الرأس متلاصقة والأصمع اللاصق أذنه برأسه والبيع جمع بيعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣalawāt refers to Jewish synagogues from the time of Moses; Kāshifī glosses the list as monks’ cells, Christian churches, and Jewish synagogues.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (صومعهاي راهبان وكليساهاي ترسايان وكنشتهاي جهودان)

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib says a worship place may be called ṣalāt, which explains the name for churches.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : يسمى موضع العبادة بالصلاة ولذلك سميت الكنائس صلوات

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some authorities regard ṣalawāt as a borrowed Syriac term, ṣlotha, meaning a prayer place.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : هي كلمة معربة وهي بالعبرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masājid refers to Muslim mosques under Muḥammad’s law; they are listed last because that dispensation came later.
rows.anchor: {ومساجد} للمسلمين في أيام شريعة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وقدم ما سوى المساجد

rows.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
rows.claim: Al-Asʾila al-Muqḥima cautions that earlier mention does not imply superiority, citing the order “some of you are disbelievers and some believers.”
rows.anchor: وفي "الأسئلة المقحمة" : تقديم الشيء بالذكر لا يدل على شرفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikran kathīran can mean remembrance repeated often or continued for a long time.
rows.anchor: أي ذكرا كثيرا أو وقتا كثيرا صفة مادحة للمساجد خصت بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may praise mosques and their people specifically, or describe all four kinds of worship places because their earlier communities remembered God there before their laws were abrogated.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون صفة للأربع لأن الذكر في الصوامع والبيع والصلوات كان معتبرا

words: وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, if God did not help hearts resist the ego, the pillars of sacred law, manners of the path, stations of reality, and mosques of the heart would be demolished; abundant remembrance needs a spacious heart lit by God.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى أنه تعالى لو لم ينصر القلوب على النفوس ويدافع عن القلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God surely aids whoever aids His friends or His religion; He fulfilled the promise by giving the Emigrants and Helpers victory over Arab, Persian, and Roman rulers and their lands.
rows.anchor: {ولينصرن الله من ينصره} أي : بالله لينصرن الله من ينصر أولياءه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is powerful over all He wills and mighty, with nothing able to resist or repel Him.
rows.anchor: {عزيز} لا يمانعه شيء ولا يدافعه

rows.speaker: بحر العلوم
rows.claim: Baḥr al-ʿUlūm says God needs no human aid to destroy His enemies; requiring believers to fight with weapons, lives, and wealth lets them gain religious and worldly benefits by obeying.
rows.anchor: وفي "بحر العلوم" : يغني بقدرته وعزته في إهلاك أعداء دينه عنهم وإنما كلفهم النصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Victory is an honored station unsuitable for unbelievers, but God alternates hardship between believers and unbelievers; otherwise faith would be forced and moral responsibility, reward, and punishment would disappear.
rows.anchor: إن النصرة والغلبة منصب شريف فلا يليق بحال الكافر لكن الله تعالى تارة يشدد المحنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tests also expiate believers’ sins, while hardship such as plague is mercy for believers but wrath and punishment for unbelievers.
rows.anchor: ولأن المؤمن قد يقدم على بعض المعاصي فيكون تشديد المحنة عليه في الدنيا كفارة له

rows.speaker: عامر
rows.claim: ʿĀmir saw a man crucified by al-Ḥajjāj and prayed that God’s forbearance not harm the oppressed; in a dream he saw the man in the highest heaven and heard that divine forbearance had placed him there.
rows.anchor: مر عامر برجل قد صلبه الحجاج قال : يا رب إن حلمك على الظالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Persian couplet portrays the earth as God’s table, with friend and foe sharing its bounty.
rows.anchor: اديم زمين سفرة عام أوست برين خوان يغماه دشمن ه دوست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each bodily member has a specific obedience; misusing it exposes a person to divine anger, as the Bustān poems warn against misusing tools, speech, hearing, and sight.
rows.anchor: ولكل عضو من أعضاء الإنسان طاعة تخصه فإذا لم يصرفه إلى مصارفه ولم يستخدمه فيما يناسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sign of a person turning to God is to use the heart for reflection on God and the afterlife, the tongue for remembrance and gratitude, and the body for service until death.
rows.anchor: يقال : علامة المنيب أي المقبل إلى الله تعالى في ثلاث خصال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī asks God to grant steadfast obedience and service and to honor the supplicants with Paradise and union.
rows.anchor: نسأل الله سبحانه أن يوفقنا لطاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every umma means a community, among past and future nations, to whom a messenger was sent.
rows.anchor: {لكل أمة} معينة من الأمم الماضية والباقية والأمة جماعة أرسل إليهم رسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mansak derives from worship and here means a particular religious law; God appointed a distinct law for each community, with no independent or shared transfer between communities.
rows.anchor: مصدر مأخوذ من النسك وهو العبادة أي شريعة خاصة لا لأمة منهم على معنى عينا كل شريعة لأمة معينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause “they perform it” reinforces exclusivity; the pronoun refers to each particular community, which alone acts according to its assigned law.
rows.anchor: صفة لمنسكا مؤكدة للقصر المستفاد من تقديم الجار والمجرور على الفعل والضمير لكل أمة باعتبار خصوصها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: From Moses to Jesus the Torah was the law, from Jesus to the Prophet the Gospel, and for the community from Muḥammad’s mission until Judgment the Qurʾān alone.
rows.anchor: من مبعث موسى إلى مبعث عيسى عليهما السلام ، منسكهم التوراة هم ناسكوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nizāʿ means pulling something from its place and hence disputing; people of other religions contemporary with the Prophet are addressed.
rows.anchor: أي : من يعاصرك من أهل الملل يقال : نزع الشيء جذبه من مقره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dispute concerns religion: other groups claim their inherited Torah or Gospel, but those laws belonged to earlier communities before abrogation; the present community has the Qurʾān alone.
rows.anchor: {فى الامر} أي : في أمر الدين زعما منهم أن شريعتهم ماعين لآبائهم الأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī’s Persian gloss emphasizes that no religious dispute is conceivable because the Prophet’s path is clearer than the sun.
rows.anchor: س بايدكه نزاع نكنند سائر أرباب اديان باتو دركار دين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is to invite all people without excluding any community, calling them to God’s oneness and worship as laid out in their law.
rows.anchor: {وادع} الناس كافة ولا تخص أمة دون أمة بالدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Straight guidance is the even path that leads to truth: the religion.
rows.anchor: أي : طريق موصل إلى الحق سوي وهو الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Then We made him” refers to humankind as a species through individuals distinct from Adam.
rows.anchor: {ثم جعلناه} أي : الجنس باعتبار أفراده

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say “him” means Adam’s offspring, with an omitted possessive; Adam himself was made from the extract of clay.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : ثم جعلناه أي نسله فحذف المضاف فيكون المراد بالإنسان آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuṭfa means clear, pure water and is also used for a man’s semen; God created the human from it.
rows.anchor: بأن خلقناه منها والنطفة الماء الصافي ويعبر بها عن ماء الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarār is a stable resting place, meaning the womb; the verbal noun is used emphatically.
rows.anchor: أي مستقر وهو الرحم عبر عنها بالقرار الذي هو مصدر مبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Makīn means secure or fortified, describing the womb by the quality of what rests inside it.
rows.anchor: أي حصين وهو وصف لها بصفة ما استقر فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God transforms the white semen into a red clot.
rows.anchor: بأن أحلنا النطفة البيضاء علقة حمراء

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib says ʿalaq is clotted blood, including the clot from which the child develops.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : العلق الدم الجامد ومنه العلقة التي يكون منها الولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A muḍgha is a morsel of flesh that could be chewed, without distinct parts or features.
rows.anchor: المضغة لحم تمضع أي فصيرناها قطعة لحم لا استبانة ولا تمايز فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greater part of the morsel becomes bones, hardened after forty-three days and arranged as the body’s central support in wise forms and positions.
rows.anchor: بأن صلبناها بعد ثلاث وأربعين وجعلناها عمودا للبدن على هيئات وأوضاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The remaining flesh covers each bone in a fitting amount and arrangement; the Persian gloss describes flesh growing over veins, limbs, tendons, and muscles.
rows.anchor: كسونا كل عظم من تلك العظام ما يليق به من اللحم على مقدار لائق به وهيئات مناسبة له

words: فَخَلَقْنَا ٱلْمُضْغَةَ عِظَٰمًۭا فَكَسَوْنَا ٱلْعِظَٰمَ لَحْمًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The differing conjunctions signal distinct transformations, and “bones” is plural because the bones vary.
rows.anchor: واختلاف العواطف للتنبيه على تفاوت الاستحالات وجمع العظام لاختلافها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brings him into another creation by breathing in the spirit; the Persian gloss continues through growth, weaning, maturity, and old age.
rows.anchor: {ثم أنشأناه} الإنشاء إيجاد الشيء وتربيته وأكثر ما يقال ذلك في الحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thumma marks the great difference between the two creations.
rows.anchor: وثم لكمال التفاوت بين الخلقين

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa argues that someone who usurps an egg and it hatches in his possession owes compensation for the egg, not the chick, since it is another creation.
rows.anchor: واحتج به أبو حنيفة رحمه الله على أن من غصب بيضة فأفرخت عنده لزمه ضمان البيضة

rows.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
rows.claim: Al-Asʾila al-Muqḥima asks why God used stages if creating humans instantly would better show power and avoid suggesting causes.
rows.anchor: قال في "الأسئلة المقحمة" : خلق الله الآدمي أطوارا ولو خلقه دفعة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response is that staged transformation displays divine power more fully: homogeneous semen becomes diverse substances and organs, each with a wondrous structure and function.
rows.anchor: فالجواب لا بل الخلق بتقليب الأعيان واختراع الأشخاص أظهر في القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevī glosses tabāraka as God’s exalted state, grounded in His comprehensive knowledge and overwhelming power.
rows.anchor: فتعالى شأنه من علمه الشامل وقدرته الباهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aḥsan al-khāliqīn is appositional to the divine name; khāliqīn means estimators, with the distinguishing noun omitted, and the excellence concerns the creation.
rows.anchor: بدل من الجلالة أي أحسن الخالقين خلقا أي المقدرين تقديرا حذف المميز لدلالة الخالقين عليه

rows.speaker: الأسئلة المقحمة
rows.claim: Al-Asʾila al-Muqḥima objects that the verse makes humans creators of their acts, with God only the best creator.
rows.anchor: وفي "الأسئلة المقحمة" : هذا يدل على أن العبد خالق أفعاله ويكون الرب أحسن منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response is that khāliqīn means image-makers: no human image-maker can equal the Creator or breathe spirit into an image; Qurʾānic khalaqa can mean forming an image.
rows.anchor: فالجواب معناه أحسن المصورين لأن المصور يصور الصورة ويشكلها

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Taʾwīlāt al-Najmiyya reads the human as a new and supremely proportioned creation, with the greatest preparedness, honor, rank, and distinction.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : {ثم خلقنا النطفة علقة} يعني خلقا غير المخلوقات

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The human is the repository of gnosis, object of divine love and care; God praises Himself at this creation because the human is the best creature.
rows.anchor: لأنه خلق أحسن المخلوقين حيث جعله معدن العرفان وموضع المحبة ومتعلق العناية

rows.speaker: المثنوي
rows.claim: The Mathnawī verses celebrate the honor of “We ennobled” and “We favored” and urge reading al-Tīn on the human’s excellent form.
rows.anchor:
وفي "المثنوي" :
أي رخ زن زهرهاست شمس الضحى
أي كداي رنك توكلكونها
تاج كرمناست بر فرق سرت
طوق فضلناست آويزبرت

rows.speaker: بعضي اهل وجدان
rows.claim: Some people of spiritual insight say humans cannot adequately praise God after their stages of growth are described, so God praises Himself in this verse.
rows.anchor: بعضي ازاهل وجدان كويندكه ون درين آيت أحوال بني آدم وترقي ازمقامي بمقامي بيان فرموده

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي سرح
rows.claim: A report says the revelation scribe ʿAbd Allāh ibn Abī Sarḥ uttered “another creation” before the Prophet dictated it, then doubted and claimed he too received revelation; the source says he either converted at the conquest or died in disbelief.
rows.anchor: روي : أن عبد الله بن أبي سرح كان يكتب لرسول الله الوحي

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: When the verse was revealed, ʿUmar independently said “Blessed is God, the best of creators”; the Prophet told him that it had been revealed in that form, and ʿUmar cherished the agreement.
rows.anchor: ولما نزلت هذه الآية قال عمر رضي الله عنه فتبارك الله أحسن الخالقين فقال عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These reports do not undermine Qurʾānic inimitability: a human’s coincident phrase is not comparable to the amount of a complete shortest sūra.
rows.anchor: لا يقال قد تكلم البشر ابتداء بمثل نظم القرآن وذلك فادح في إعجازه لما أن الخارج عن قدرة البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lafḥ means that fire burns with its heat; al-Qāmūs glosses it as burning, and al-Irshād says it is more forceful than nafḥ.
rows.anchor: {تلفح وجوههم النار} تحرقها يقال : لفحته النار بحرها أحرقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faces are singled out as the noblest and most protected members, making their punishment a stronger deterrent; they precede the agent in the wording.
rows.anchor: وتخصيص الوجوه بذلك لأنها أشرف الأعضاء وأعظم ما يصان منها فبيان حالها أزجر عن المعاصي المؤدية إلى النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāliḥūn means their lips shrink back from their teeth in the intense burning, like roasted heads.
rows.anchor: والكلوح تقلص الشفتين عن الأسنان كما ترى الرؤوس المشوية

rows.speaker: مالك بن دينار
rows.claim: Mālik ibn Dīnār says ʿUtba the young ascetic repented after seeing a head taken from an oven; he fainted for three days and nights.
rows.anchor: وعن مالك بن دينار كان سبب توبة عتبة الغلام أنه مر في السوق برأس أخرج من التنور

rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: A hadith describes the fire drawing the upper lip to the middle of the head and letting the lower lip hang to the navel.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "تشويه النار فتقلص شفته العليا حتى تبلغ وسط رأسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned are addressed by way of reproach, rebuke, and reminding them why they deserved the punishment they suffer.
rows.anchor: فيقال لهم تعنيفا وتوبيخا وتذكيرا لما به استحقوا ما ابتلوا به من العذاب
